issues.title: Discrete source-operator interface

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given \({\bf F}= (g,f) \in {\bf \mathds{W}}\), the discrete source problem associated with \eqref{a3.3}

issues.failure_explanation: The input F in a3.5 is uniformly allowed to be any element of W=L2×L2. Only its L2 projection is available for such data; the stabilization S_b, implemented through the virtual-element degrees of freedom chi, is not defined on an arbitrary L2 representative. Thus b_h(F,Psi_h), and hence the advertised source-problem input-output contract, is not well defined. The subsequent equation using b(F,Psi_h) is well defined but corresponds to a different mass form from both a3.5 and the discrete eigenproblem a3.3.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenproblem a3.3 remains defined for discrete arguments, but its claimed source and adjoint operators on W are not coherently defined. Consequently the source-error estimates and the operator-convergence bridge used for the eigenspace, eigenvalue, and eigenfunction estimates are not established by the old construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the discrete eigenproblem a3.3 unchanged and define the b_h source and adjoint solves initially only for data in V_h, yielding an operator \widetilde{A}_h on V_h. For F=(g,f) in W, let Q_h be the L2 projection onto the scalar virtual-element space, lift F to P_hF=(Q_hf,Q_hf) in V_h, and define A_h=\widetilde{A}_hP_h, with the analogous adjoint construction. Verify that this reproduces the discrete b_h right-hand side and hence the nonzero spectrum and eigenfunctions of a3.3. Then replace every invalid use of b_h(F,·) in Lemmas 3.3–3.4 by the projected right-hand side and propagate the resulting mass-consistency bounds through operator convergence and the listed spectral estimates without changing their rates.
issues.why_classification: The degree-of-freedom stabilization cannot act on arbitrary L2 data, while simply replacing b_h by b defines a different operator from the discrete eigenproblem, so no transcriptional or one-line repair suffices. A complete repair requires a new ambient-space projection/extension, a spectrum-equivalence check, and corresponding source-consistency estimates. This is a contained construction within the existing source-operator and spectral framework and preserves the method and rates, so it is moderate rather than serious, but it exceeds a routine minor repair.

issues.title: Missing reverse-consistency term

failure_location.quote: a_h({\bf U}^{\bf F}_h-{\bf U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_I-{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi) - a({\bf U}^{\bf F}_h-{\bf U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_I-{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi)  + a_h({\bf U}^{\bf F}_{h},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi) - a({\bf U}^{\bf F}_{h},{\boldsymbol \Phi}_\pi).

issues.failure_explanation: In Lemma 3.3, U_pi and Phi_pi are elementwise polynomial while Phi_I is virtual, and n is only assumed piecewise smooth, not elementwise constant. Expanding the old right-hand side gives D_h(U_h,Phi_I)-D_h(U_pi,Phi_I), since D_h(U_pi,Phi_pi)=0. Hence the asserted equality omits D_h(U_pi,Phi_I). For variable n, its weighted mass contribution contains the pairing of the projection residual of n w_pi with the virtual residual of phi_I and need not vanish. Equations a3.6 and a3.15 provide consistency only in the opposite argument orientation.
issues.overall_effect: The L2 source estimate in Lemma 3.3 is not proved over the claimed piecewise-smooth variable-coefficient class. Lemma 3.4 repeats the same zero treatment and relies on Lemma 3.3, so the ensuing operator, eigenspace, eigenvalue, and eigenfunction estimates are also unestablished until the reverse term is controlled. The obstruction disappears in the elementwise-constant special case but not in the full stated regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let D_h=a_h-a and correct the decomposition to include D_h(U_π,Φ_I): D_h(U_h,Φ_I)=D_h(U_h-U_π,Φ_I-Φ_π)+D_h(U_h,Φ_π)+D_h(U_π,Φ_I), using D_h(U_π,Φ_π)=0. Establish the reverse-consistency estimate |D_h(U_π,Φ_h)| ≲ ‖n w_π-Π_l^0(n w_π)‖_0‖φ_h-Π_l^0φ_h‖_0, and use it wherever the polynomial-first consistency defect was set to zero in Lemmas 3.3–3.4 and the listed spectral estimates. The existing approximation assumptions then place the added residuals at the same or higher order, preserving all stated rates.
issues.why_classification: This is not a typo because the proof actually discards a generally nonzero term and must justify its control. Nevertheless, the required reverse estimate follows directly from L2-projection orthogonality and Cauchy–Schwarz, exactly parallel to the existing forward-consistency estimate a3.15. Carrying the resulting higher-order residual through the affected proofs is routine and requires no new assumptions, architecture, or loss of conclusions or rates, so the issue is minor.
